description: Found by Elixir Parity (2026-11-20). `import Mod` inside a def body fails with 'unsupported expression prefix in compiler2 front door: Import'. Elixir allows lexical import, require and alias in function bodies, scoped to the rest of the body. Once it works, a def emitted by an item macro can hold a macro call only the body expander expands; fz-mue.38's disjoint counter ranges already cover that. Owner: Elixir Parity. Related: fz-p8p.21 (ambiguous imports).

comments.text: User approved page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-mue.43.html (2026-11-24), with all recommendations. The expander owns body scope: a block walk rebinds the namespace per statement; nested blocks inherit and don't export; calls resolved through a body import get __fz_bound__ stamped; a body alias is rewritten to its module; __ENV__/__CALLER__ are projected from the lexical scope; ScopeSession's apply_alias/import/require become shared functions. Two commits: (1) parse import/require/alias as expressions (unblocks quote in __using__), (2) the scope walk. In scope: same-module re-import replaces (at module level too), plus the options warn:, only: :macros, alias A.{B,C}, require M, as:. Out of scope: unused import/alias warnings, a separate ticket at the epic's end (proposed via Coordinator); ambiguity is fz-p8p.21. Fixtures 01940-01941.

title: import, require and alias work inside a function body, as in Elixir
